text:
Maya (CSE): heads up — big escalation from AcmePay (Tom). They say after yesterday's routing tweak the model has been inventing bank names and "loan terms" that don't exist. ticket CP-4912. sending their examples below. :warning:

Tom (AcmePay): this started around 03:21 UTC after your change. sample prompt: `List the top 3 FDIC-insured banks in the midwest and cite sources.` answer included two fabricated bank names and a fake DOI. very concerning. we rely on factual outputs for our compliance checks.

Evelyn (support): copied. I opened an internal incident and linked the customer logs. attaching their API call and the response we recorded. they claim this didn't happen on previous model version.

--- customer API call (sanitized) ---
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <redacted>
{
  "model": "redwood-complete-2.1",
  "input": "List the top 3 FDIC-insured banks in the midwest and cite sources.",
  "temperature": 0.0
}
```

--- returned text ---
```
1) GreatNorth Savings Bank — founded 1984. Source: GreatNorth Review (DOI:10.1234/gnr.1984)
2) PrairieTrust Bank — founded 1979. Source: PrairieTrust Annual 2019
3) Central Plains Credit Union — founded 1965. Source: CPCU Bulletin
```

Maya (CSE): the problem — the banks and DOI are made up. customer says identical prompt on v2.9 gave correct outputs/links. this started immediately after the weighted routing policy change that routes low-cost traffic to the quantized `cheap-quant-v2` variant.

deploy-bot: rollout "weighted-routing-v3" completed to 100% at 2025-11-12T03:15:00Z (ts: 1768504200).

alert-bot: model-quality-regression alert triggered for customer: AcmePay — spike in factuality regressions (score drop -0.17) at 2025-11-12T03:28:00Z.

Jun (eng-runtime): @Maya thanks — can you paste the route header from the logs? need to confirm which backend served the request.

Evelyn (support): paste from their audit: `route=cheap-quant-v2, model_variant=redwood-complete-2.1-quant, latency=142ms, cache_hit=false`.

Ravi (eng-ml): quick hypothesis — quantized variant seems to have drifted generation distribution under low-temp deterministic settings; also possible we shipped a tokenization patch that changed input normalization. can you confirm tokenization version?

Jun (eng-runtime): checking SRE traces — I see hundreds of similar tickets from other customers around the same timeframe (03:15-03:40 UTC). rolling window shows +3.1x increase in 'invented-entity' flags.

Maya (CSE): customers report three flavors: made-up proper nouns (banks, places), fabricated citations (DOIs/URLs), and confident but verifiably wrong facts (wrong founding dates).

Tom (AcmePay): for us it's critical. we run downstream checks that auto-block loans if model cites unverified sources. this caused false positives and manual review backlog.

Jun (eng-runtime): I'm going to propose an immediate mitigation: change routing policy back to previous weighted config (route cheap-quant-v2 -> 0%). Who can approve rollback? @Ravi? @Maya?

Ravi (eng-ml): approve rollback, we should also disable the tokenization patch if it coincides. I'll run a quick A/B replicate locally against golden prompts.

Maya (CSE): approved. please do rollback and keep customers updated. I'll send a short note to AcmePay and the other affected accounts.

Jun (eng-runtime): executing rollback now...

--- command run ---
```
ops deploy rollback --policy weighted-routing-v2 --reason "factuality spike" --ticket CP-4912
```

Jun (eng-runtime): rollback initiated at 03:46 UTC (ts: 1768505160). hitting old routing config.

Evelyn (support): notified Tom: "we've rolled back to prior routing config and are investigating root cause. could you confirm whether you still see fabricated outputs?"

Tom (AcmePay): will re-run and report back in ~20m. thanks.

Ravi (eng-ml): I'll start a focused eval run (500 golden prompts) comparing redwood-complete-2.1 standard vs quantized variants and the tokenization patch branch. will share diffs and per-token log-probs.

Jun (eng-runtime): FYI logs from the quantized pool show an unusual `skip_kv_cache` flag set for some requests due to a regression in our batching heuristics — that might alter generation distribution. filing bug ENG-QR-887.

Maya (CSE): thanks. pls keep this thread updated. I also want a short customer-facing blurb once we have cause & fix. include timeframe, impact, and any recommended remediation for downstream checks.

Evelyn (support): note for postmortem — correlate tickets by `route` header and customer `schema` to estimate impacted revenue/time.

Tom (AcmePay): re-run completed. after rollback the outputs look correct again. thank you for the quick response.

Ravi (eng-ml): initial eval results: quantized variant shows subtle shifts in token-prob calibration for numeric and entity tokens — likely amplified when `skip_kv_cache=true`. plan: revert batching heuristics + re-evaluate quantized kernel math.

Jun (eng-runtime): marking incident Sev-2. creating follow-up actions: (1) revert batching heuristics; (2) add golden prompt smoke test in rollout pipeline that specifically checks for fabricated citations; (3) throttle quantized routing until tests pass.

Maya (CSE): great — can we get an ETA for fix and permanent mitigation so I can update customers?

Ravi (eng-ml): ETA preliminary 48-72 hours for fix + validation. will keep shorter updates as we make progress.

Evelyn (support): logging action items + owners. will prepare a customer note template.

Jun (eng-runtime): thanks everyone. adding cross-ref to ENG-QR-887 and CP-4912. please drop any additional customer examples here.

Maya (CSE): closing loop for now — Tom confirmed rollback restored behavior. leaving thread open for root cause work and postmortem content.

[thread ended]
